info.name: TraceLit API v2
info.description:
## TraceLit — Intelligent Academic Literature Assistant

Sentence-level verified attribution and confidence scoring for multi-document QA.

**Base URL:** `{{base_url}}{{api_prefix}}`  (default: `http://localhost:8000/api/v1`)

---

## Quickstart Flow

```
1.  GET  /health                              Health check
2.  POST /sessions                            Create session      → session_id
3.  POST /sessions/{id}/papers               Upload PDFs         → paper_id
4.  WS   /ws/{id}                            Monitor processing  (WebSocket)
5.  POST /sessions/{id}/chat                 Chat with papers
6.  POST /sessions/{id}/compare              Compare papers
7.  GET  /sessions/{id}/analysis/gaps        Research gap analysis
8.  GET  /sessions/{id}/analysis/review      Literature review
9.  POST /sessions/{id}/export               Export results
10. POST /verify/{session_id}               Standalone HAVF verify
```

---

## Auto-Captured Environment Variables

| Variable | Set by | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | Create Session | Session UUID |
| `paper_id` | Upload Papers | First paper UUID |
| `second_paper_id` | Upload Papers | Second paper UUID |
| `export_filename` | Export requests | Generated filename |

---

## HAVF Confidence Levels

| Level | Embedding Score | Algorithm |
|---|---|---|
| `HIGH` | >= 0.85 | Level 1: fast embedding similarity |
| `MEDIUM` | 0.65–0.84 | Level 2: cross-encoder reranking |
| `LOW` | < 0.65 | No reliable source found |

---

## Paper Processing Stages

`pending` → `processing` → `ready` | `failed`

Stages: `extraction` → `chunking` → `embedding` → `indexing`

request.description:
Permanently delete a session and **all associated data**: papers, sentence chunks, FAISS vectors, and exported files.

⚠️ This action is irreversible.

**Response:** `204 No Content`

Returns the WebSocket (`ws://` or `wss://`) URL for real-time paper processing progress.

The scheme is derived from the incoming HTTP request (`http` → `ws`, `https` → `wss`).

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `websocket_url` | string | Full WebSocket URL to connect to |
| `session_id` | string | Echo of the session UUID |

**WebSocket events after connecting:**

```json
{ "type": "paper_progress",  "paper_id": "...", "progress": 0.42, "stage": "embedding", "eta_seconds": 18 }
{ "type": "paper_completed", "paper_id": "..." }
{ "type": "paper_failed",    "paper_id": "...", "error": "PDF is password-protected" }
```

item.name: 📄 Papers
item.description: Upload, list, inspect, and delete PDF papers within a session. Papers are processed asynchronously — monitor progress via WebSocket or poll Get Paper.

formdata.description: Select 1–7 PDF files. Each must be ≤ 50 MB.

request.description:
Upload 1–7 PDF files to the session. Each file is validated, saved to disk, and queued for async background processing.

**Processing pipeline per paper:**
1. PDF text extraction (page-by-page)
2. Section detection and sentence-aware chunking
3. Sentence embedding (local model)
4. FAISS vector indexing
5. Metadata extraction (title, authors, year, abstract)

**Constraints:**
- `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`
- Form field name must be `files` (repeat field for multiple files)
- Only `.pdf` extension accepted
- Maximum 7 files per request
- Maximum 50 MB per file

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `paper_ids` | string[] | UUIDs for all registered papers |
| `message` | string | Human-readable confirmation |

> The test script stores the first two paper IDs as `paper_id` and `second_paper_id`.

response.name: 201 Created

400 Too Many Files
400 File Too Large

item.name: 💬 Chat
item.description: RAG-based question answering over uploaded papers. Every response sentence passes the HAVF verification pipeline and is tagged HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW confidence.

request.description:
Send a natural-language query and receive a verified, cited answer as a single JSON response.

**Pipeline per request:**
1. Query is embedded → top-k sentence chunks retrieved from FAISS
2. Context assembled → sent to LLM (Gemini → Groq → Ollama fallback)
3. LLM must cite every sentence with `[P#]` paragraph tags
4. Citation IDs validated against indexed paragraphs
5. Each sentence passes HAVF (embedding similarity + optional cross-encoder)
6. Message persisted to session chat history

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | **Yes** | 1–5000 chars |
| `stream` | bool | No | `false` for sync JSON (default) |

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | string | Full answer with `[P#]` citation tags |
| `provider` | string | LLM used: `gemini` \| `groq` \| `ollama` |
| `havf_results` | array | Per-sentence verification (see below) |
| `token_count` | int | Tokens consumed by LLM |
| `latency_ms` | float | End-to-end latency in ms |

**HAVF result fields per sentence:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | string | The verified sentence |
| `confidence` | string | `HIGH` \| `MEDIUM` \| `LOW` |
| `score` | float | Best cosine similarity score 0.0–1.0 |
| `source_sentence` | string\|null | Most similar source sentence |
| `paragraph_id` | string\|null | Cited paragraph ID, e.g. `P5` |
| `sentence_key` | string\|null | Internal sentence identifier |

> Requires at least one paper with `status = ready`.

request.description:
Streaming variant of Send Message. Uses a **dedicated /chat/stream endpoint** and returns **Server-Sent Events (SSE)**.

**SSE event types:**

| Event | Description |
|---|---|
| `query_type` | Query classification (SIMPLE_QA, COMPARISON, etc.) |
| `sources` | Retrieved source chunks |
| `token` | Incremental LLM text chunk |
| `havf` | HAVF verification results after all tokens |
| `done` | Final event: provider, full text, token count, latency |
| `error` | Unrecoverable error |

**SSE format example:**

```
data: {"type": "query_type", "query_type": "SIMPLE_QA"}
data: {"type": "sources", "sources": [...]}
data: {"type": "token", "content": "Transformer"}
data: {"type": "token", "content": " models"}
...
data: {"type": "havf", "havf_results": [...]}
data: {"type": "done", "provider": "gemini", "token_count": 312, "latency_ms": 1842.5}
```

> ⚠️ Postman HTTP runner has limited SSE support. Use the browser `EventSource` API or `curl --no-buffer` for best results.

response.name: 200 OK (SSE stream)

item.name: 📊 Analysis
item.description: Higher-level analysis across papers: keyword extraction, research gap detection, and automatic literature review generation.

request.description:
Extract the most significant keywords from a single paper with relevance scores.

Keywords are derived from TF-IDF scoring over indexed sentence chunks.

**Path parameters:**
- `session_id` — session UUID
- `paper_id` — paper UUID (must be `status = ready`)

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `paper_id` | string | Paper UUID |
| `keywords` | array | `{keyword, score}` objects ordered by relevance (desc) |

**Keyword object:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `keyword` | string | Extracted keyword or keyphrase |
| `score` | float | Relevance score 0.0–1.0 |

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Analyse all ready papers in the session to identify research themes and highlight underexplored areas (gaps).

**Algorithm:**
1. Aggregate keywords from all ready papers
2. Cluster into high-level themes
3. Compute per-theme coverage ratio (fraction of papers addressing it)
4. Flag low-coverage themes as potential research gaps

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `themes` | array | All detected themes with coverage data |
| `underexplored` | array | Subset: low-coverage themes (gaps) |

**Theme object:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | Theme name |
| `keywords` | string[] | Representative keywords |
| `papers_covering` | string[]\|null | Paper UUIDs that address this theme |
| `coverage_ratio` | float | 0.0–1.0 fraction of papers covering this theme |

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Generate a coherent mini literature review synthesising all ready papers in the session.

The LLM receives each paper's contributions and keywords and writes a structured review: background, methodological landscape, comparative findings, and open questions.

**Response fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `review` | string | Full literature review text (markdown) |
| `paper_count` | int | Number of papers included |
| `provider` | string | LLM provider used |

item.name: ✅ Verification
item.description: Standalone HAVF verification. Check arbitrary text (your notes, external summaries, or LLM outputs from other tools) against indexed papers for sentence-level attribution confidence.

request.description:
Verify arbitrary text against one or more indexed papers using the HAVF pipeline.

**Path parameters:**
- `session_id` — session UUID (validates paper ownership)

Each sentence in `text` is independently evaluated.

**HAVF algorithm:**

**Level 1 (~5ms, handles ~89% of cases):**
- Embed sentence → cosine similarity vs all source sentences in indexed papers
- Score >= 0.85 → `HIGH` (return immediately)
- Score 0.65–0.84 → proceed to Level 2
- Score < 0.65 → `LOW` (return immediately)

**Level 2 (~40ms, uncertain cases only):**
- Cross-encoder reranking of top candidate source sentences
- Score >= 0.75 → `MEDIUM`
- Score < 0.75 → `LOW`

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | **Yes** | 1–10000 chars. One or more sentences. |
| `paper_ids` | string[] | **Yes** | 1+ UUIDs of `ready` papers |

**Response:** Array of `VerificationItem`:

**HAVF result fields per sentence:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | string | The verified sentence |
| `confidence` | string | `HIGH` \| `MEDIUM` \| `LOW` |
| `score` | float | Best cosine similarity score 0.0–1.0 |
| `source_sentence` | string\|null | Most similar source sentence |
| `paragraph_id` | string\|null | Cited paragraph ID, e.g. `P5` |
| `sentence_key` | string\|null | Internal sentence identifier |

response.name: 200 OK
422 Validation Error

item.name: 🔌 WebSocket
item.description: Real-time paper processing progress. Use Postman's WebSocket tab (New > WebSocket Request) to connect — standard HTTP requests cannot upgrade to WebSocket.

request.description:
WebSocket endpoint for real-time paper processing progress updates.

**⚠️ This is a WebSocket URL. Open Postman → New → WebSocket Request.**

The WebSocket is mounted at the app root (`/ws`), **not** under `/api/v1`.

---

## Connection Steps

1. Call `GET /sessions/{session_id}/ws-url` to get the exact URL
2. Open Postman → **New → WebSocket Request**
3. Paste the returned `websocket_url` and click **Connect**

Or use: `{{ws_base_url}}/ws/{{session_id}}`

---

## Incoming Events

**Connected:**
```json
{ "type": "connected", "connection_id": "..." }
```

**Progress update:**
```json
{ "type": "paper_progress", "paper_id": "...", "progress": 0.42, "stage": "embedding", "eta_seconds": 18 }
```

**Paper ready:**
```json
{ "type": "paper_completed", "paper_id": "..." }
```

**Paper failed:**
```json
{ "type": "paper_failed", "paper_id": "...", "error": "PDF is password-protected" }
```

**Paper deleted:**
```json
{ "type": "paper_deleted", "paper_id": "...", "session_id": "..." }
```

**Session deleted:**
```json
{ "type": "session_deleted", "session_id": "..." }
```

---

## Heartbeat

The server sends a `ping` event every 30 seconds. Send the text message `ping` — the server replies with a JSON `pong`.

---

## Processing Stages

| Stage | Description |
|---|---|
| `extraction` | Extracting text from PDF pages |
| `chunking` | Splitting into sentence-aware chunks |
| `embedding` | Generating sentence embeddings |
| `indexing` | Writing vectors to FAISS index |
